verses.sa: प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः । यः पश्यति तथाऽऽत्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति ॥
verses.tr: One who sees all actions as being done only by nature, and sees the true self as the non-doer, sees rightly.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is teaching Arjuna about the difference between the field and the knower of the field, and here he explains who really performs all actions.

body.text: One who sees all actions as being done only by nature, and sees the true self as the non-doer, sees rightly. The verse repeats the word pashyati, sees, to show that true vision is seeing two things at once: the body-mind acts through prakrti, while the atma remains akartaram, a non-doer. Next Krishna describes how this true vision grows into seeing all beings rooted in one source.

verses.sa: यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति । तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा ॥
verses.tr: When one sees all beings as rooted in one nature and all expansion arising from that source, one attains the supreme reality.
verses.angle: Seeing two things at once: root and spread
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna carries on by showing how to see the whole picture instead of just the parts. Listen to the two acts of seeing in this verse.

body.text: When one sees all beings as rooted in one nature and all expansion arising from that source, one attains the supreme reality. The verse pairs two acts of seeing. First, you see the separate states of beings resting in one place, and then you see their expansion. Seeing both together is what carries you to the supreme reality. Krishna now names the supreme self, calling it beginningless, beyond the gunas, and beyond action.

verses.sa: अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्मायमव्ययः । शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते ॥
verses.tr: O son of Kunti, this supreme self is beginningless, beyond the gunas, and imperishable. Though abiding in the body, it does not act and is not stained.
verses.angle: the self is untouched even while in the body
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the source of all expansion. Now he asks you to look at the self that lives inside the body. What is its nature?

body.text: O son of Kunti, this supreme self is beginningless, beyond the gunas, and imperishable. Though abiding in the body, it does not act and is not stained. The verse tells you this self is beginningless and beyond the gunas, and even while it lives in a body, it does not act and is not stained. Krishna explains that just as space is untouched by what happens within it, the self remains pure in every body.

verses.sa: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते । सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥
verses.tr: As all-pervading space is not tainted because of its subtlety, so the self, present in every body, is not tainted.
verses.angle: Self dwells in body without being stained
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna explains the true self inside the body using the image of space. Listen to how he shows the self remains untouched.

body.text: As all-pervading space is not tainted because of its subtlety, so the self, present in every body, is not tainted. Space is everywhere and stays untouched because it is subtle, and the self in every body is the same. The next verse brings in the sun, showing how the knower of the field lights up the whole field.

verses.sa: यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः । क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत ॥
verses.tr: As one sun illuminates this whole world, so the knower of the field illuminates the whole field, O Bharata.
verses.angle: eka: the one who lights everything
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for the word that reveals who is doing the illuminating here.

body.text: As one sun illuminates this whole world, so the knower of the field illuminates the whole field, O Bharata. Notice the verb prakashayati, illuminates. The knower of the field is not a passive witness; it actively illuminates the whole field, just as the sun lights the world. Krishna now turns to the eye of wisdom that allows us to distinguish between the field and the knower of the field.

verses.sa: क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा । भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम् ॥
verses.tr: In this way, those who know the distinction between the field and the knower of the field with the eye of wisdom, and who know release from the source of nature, attain the supreme.
verses.angle: knowledge-eye separates the knower from the field
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is teaching the final truth, that the knower and the known must be seen as different. Listen for the two things a person must know to reach the supreme.

body.text: In this way, those who know the distinction between the field and the knower of the field with the eye of wisdom, and who know release from the source of nature, attain the supreme. Krishna pairs the eye of knowledge with release from nature. He says the supreme is reached by those who know the difference between the field and the knower and also know how to free themselves from material nature. Krishna says he will speak again of this highest knowledge, which sages have used to reach the supreme perfection.

prev.title: Nature, the self, and the one who sees
